tradition.name: Experimental Big Band
tradition.lineage: Experimental Big Band extends large-ensemble jazz through collective improvisation, unconventional orchestration and the meeting of composed structures with open forms. Free-jazz orchestras and later creative big bands offer different approaches within this field.

extras.description: Contrasting reed registers, low winds and rhythm-section textures can build dense collective passages or open into sparse exchanges. Sectional writing and individual improvisation interact, with some ensembles also drawing on rock or minimalism.

entries.geo_rationale: Issuer explicitly locates original three-track May1968 recording at Lila Eule in Bremen; city-level approximate point, not exact venue coordinates or exclusive genre origin.

instrument_role_audit.scope: Peter Brötzmann Octet — Machine Gun, complete original three-track1968 album program (Machine Gun; Responsible / For Jan Van De Ven; Music for Han Bennink), preserved as tracks1–3 of the official FMP2025 remaster. No claim all registers sound simultaneously throughout.

tradition.name: Funk das Antigas
tradition.lineage: Funk das antigas keeps earlier Brazilian funk circulating through heritage bailes, DJs, dance groups and intergenerational celebrations. Funk melody, familiar MC refrains and older sound-system repertoire meet in a living culture of musical memory.

extras.description: DJs connect familiar beats and refrains for shared dancing, while recurring passinho gatherings pass on movements and repertoire. Romantic songs and more forceful MC material coexist; live singers also participate in the wider revival circuit.

entries.geo_rationale: Official municipality documents recurring contemporary dance practice here. This is an editorial practice anchor within the wider Rio-state/Brazilian field, not an exclusive origin claim.
entries.model_policy: Representative DJ selection/mixing branch positively documented by the municipality and heritage festival organizers. It preserves all recorded beats, melodies, sampled refrains and voices without guessing their generators. No claim that the whole broader field has no live MCs, or that this model reconstructs every festival role. Dance teacher/audience activity does not establish another musical sound-source card. Live singer count and embedded voices remain unknown. Controlled live-room presentation is authored; no source decks, global tuning, exact tempo or auditioned tracklist asserted. The literal up-tempo output is an authored brisk dance rendition consistent with the reported lively baile, not a measured tempo of all older recordings.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Actual full baile_funk already includes melô-rap, funk melody, later proibidão and modern variants; historical repertoire alone is not a new boundary. Funk das Antigas is an ongoing narrower heritage-circulation practice within that broad field: municipal recurrent teaching groups, funded named bailes and festival projects explicitly organize preservation and transmission across generations. It overlaps funk_melody but is not confined to that romantic sung substyle; the creator corpus also includes MCs and sound-system material beyond it. Exact community identity rests on institutional primary evidence, not different artists or an arbitrary date cutoff. No exclusive sonic grammar or alias claimed.

tradition.name: Plug Brasileiro
tradition.lineage: Plug brasileiro connects Brazilian rappers and producers through internet releases, melodic experimentation and self-produced beats. The local network adapts the spacious beat vocabulary of plugg to Portuguese-language expression, with some artists also drawing on samba, arrocha and other Brazilian song forms.

extras.description: Rapped phrases and melodic inflections sit over spacious produced beats. Online collaboration and independent releases connect a Brazilian network whose music ranges from understated reflection to playful crossovers with local popular styles.

entries.geo_rationale: Firsthand artist interview identifies Irajá, Rio de Janeiro, upbringing and local rap influences; editorial network anchor, not an exclusive genre origin.

extras.description: An agile rapped lead rides a produced beat, with recurring rhythmic phrases and room for spontaneous cadences. The wider repertoire links dance hooks, melodic crossover and colorful electronic production.

entries.geo_rationale: Firsthand producer and rapper interviews explicitly place this creative network in Atlanta; approximate community anchor, not an exact recording address.
entries.model_policy: Authored solo accompanied rap branch grounded in Zaytoven’s firsthand account of Yung L.A. improvising words over supplied beats at home. This is general documented practice, not a reconstruction of Ain’t I or any group recording. Natural rhythmic spoken lead, moderate effort and close dry studio are editable arrangement choices. Full produced accompaniment retained by existing credited beat identity; no invented synth, sample, drum hardware or master stems. tradition.name: GbVfi

tradition.name: Corrosion
tradition.lineage: Corrosion connects gothic-rock and darkwave bands carrying the melodic, atmospheric side of post-punk into later independent scenes. Expressive singing, interlocking electric guitars and bass combine with keyboards and programmed rhythms, supporting songs of melancholy, romantic tension and nocturnal imagery.

extras.description: Layered vocal and keyboard textures frame recurring guitar figures and a firm bass foundation. Programmed percussion can give the songs a regular pulse, while darker harmonies and spacious arrangements link contemporary recordings to the gothic-rock revival.

extras.description: Lead and supporting voices meet ringing electric guitar, bass, drums and synthesizer color. Recurring hooks and a buoyant pulse give the songs a direct, danceable character while a live band supplies dynamic accents.

tradition.name: Modern Dream Pop
tradition.lineage: Modern dream pop extends atmospheric independent pop through intimate singing, repeating melodic figures and richly layered guitar, keyboard and electronic textures. Its contemporary bands and solo artists revisit earlier dream-pop and shoegaze approaches while circulating through independent labels, concerts and streaming communities.

extras.description: Suspended melodic phrases and recurring harmonies give the songs a hazy, reflective character. Piano interpretations place melody and accompaniment together on one keyboard, while the broader repertoire also uses voices, guitars, organs, synthesizers and programmed or live rhythms.

tradition.name: Classic Tollywood
tradition.lineage: Classic Tollywood gathers familiar Telugu-language film songs and the playback voices and composers who keep them in circulation. Memorable melodic refrains, expressive diction and contrasting verse sections link romantic songs, dance numbers and classical-inflected compositions across film generations.

extras.description: Playback singing places the melody and Telugu text at the center, with orchestral, band and electronic arrangements varying across the repertoire. Vocal renditions also carry these songs into lessons and informal performance, where phrasing, breath and small melodic ornaments shape a familiar tune.

tradition.name: Música Sinaloense
tradition.lineage: Música Sinaloense gathers popular repertoires associated with Sinaloa, including corridos, romantic song, norteño and guitar-led regional groups alongside the state’s celebrated wind bands. Contemporary artists connect local song traditions with pop-facing melodies and circulated recordings.

extras.description: Expressive singing and recurring refrains carry narratives and romantic themes. Guitar rhythm and answering accordion phrases form one small-group setting, while brass bands and other string-led ensembles supply contrasting textures across the wider regional repertoire.

sources.support: Exact named creator corpus and LaReceta37.
Own artist PR release19Dec2024 by The3Collective, names Culiacán group and guitars/accordions with pop-ballad/norteño song approach.
Firsthand band interview about regional corrido practice and festival presentation.

entries.model_policy: Representative contemporary Sinaloan regional-song arrangement with singing, guitars and accordion, the three positive musical roles named in La Receta’s own December2024 agency release for Sálvame. This is a new genre-practice arrangement, not an exhaustive transcription or stem inventory of that commercial master. Multiple guitars share one family with the same authored settings; no exact source headcount or undocumented original instrument architecture is asserted. A six-string steel dreadnought with Engelmann top, rosewood back/sides,80/20strings and ringing strums supplies chordal support; a steel-reed LMM accordion with light demi-swing tremolo, articulated bellows, cardboard/leather bellows and no cassotto supplies answering phrases. These meaningful physical choices are authored rather than attributed to the band. Singing is natural syllabic solo lead with physiology unspecified. Functional-harmonic verse–chorus–bridge organization is explicitly authored; source pop-ballad/norteño connection remains candid. No brass band recording is reduced to these roles, and no claim that all source-master production is exhaustively credited is made. The new representative rendition intentionally uses a brisk sung pulse with rolling duple accordion accompaniment. This is an authored norteño-facing arrangement of the documented guitar/accordion song practice, not a measured tempo or rhythmic transcription of Sálvame. The actual klezmer-dancing label is assessed through its full note, rolling oompah that wants both feet at once: that accompaniment gesture is compatible with this intended duple branch. No Jewish heritage, klezmer ornament system or repertoire is being attributed to La Receta; independent review must judge the full literal context, not accept based only on this disclaimer.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Full banda_sinaloense already names Sinaloa’s wind-band tradition with brass/percussion and ranchera/corrido/cumbia repertoire. The actual Música Sinaloense creator cohort also includes contemporary guitar-led and norteño-facing groups; this named regional discovery field overlaps banda, corrido, norteño and musica_mexicana rather than asserting they exclude Sinaloa. The selected small-group song branch does not define a universal regional ensemble or prove an exclusive sonic category.

tradition.name: Nova Música Paulista
tradition.lineage: Nova música paulista connects contemporary São Paulo songwriting with independent musical networks and a wide range of Brazilian and international influences. Artists move between intimate song, samba-related rhythms, pop, jazz, experimental textures and electronic production, sustaining a varied metropolitan scene.

extras.description: Expressive singing and distinctive songwriting link arrangements of many sizes. In the voice-and-guitar branch, ringing chords and melodic accompaniment leave room for lyrical detail, flexible phrasing and contrasts between reflective passages and rhythmic refrains.

sources.support: Complete exact named creator100; broad corpus and direct Tulipa membership.
Municipal presenter explicitly names nova música paulista and Tulipa, Mariana Aydar, Thiago Pethit and Raf Vilar, with pop/folk/jazz breadth.
Complete presenter announcement explicitly voice-and-guitar performance across four albums.
Institutional retrospective confirms31July2022 voice-and-guitar concert.
Contemporary firsthand critical listening identifies GustavoRuiz featured solo on instrumental jazzy samba-choro Passeio; separate broader guitarist practice, not museum setlist/roster.

entries.model_policy: The representative voice-and-guitar branch is positively documented by the Museu da Língua Portuguesa for Tulipa and Gustavo Ruiz’s31July2022 performance, revisiting songs from four albums, and its subsequent institutional activity report confirms the event. It is not a claim that those complete studio albums contain only two roles: percussion and other production on TU or other editions are not omitted from an asserted master. One accompanied natural syllabic singer and one standard six-string nylon guitar are the authored rendition. Guitar architecture is unspecified by the programme; cedar top, fan bracing, carbon strings, standard tuning, ringing chord strums and rest-stroke bass notes are candid representative construction/technique choices, not measured Gustavo equipment. The selected functional-harmonic verse–chorus–bridge organization is authored, not a transcription of every song. No fixed original tempo or one universal mood is asserted. This new authored duo rendition uses brisk, conversational nylon-guitar interplay, with choro-influenced answering and bass motion around the sung melody. Context is positive rather than geography alone: the same guitarist Gustavo Ruiz is independently heard soloing on the jazzy samba-choro Passeio in Junio Barreto’s2004 album, documented by a contemporary firsthand listening review. That evidence supports his broader performed vocabulary, not a claim that the2022 museum duo set played Passeio or the exact same accompaniment. The source seven-string guitar on another album track is not attributed to this source-unspecified duo guitar. A standard six-string realization remains candidly authored. No other players from the separate Barreto album are omitted from an asserted reconstruction.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Full nova_mpb already includes Tulipa Ruiz and São Paulo as well as Rio/Brasília, so substantial overlap is explicit. Its quiet intimate post2008 songwriter definition does not exhaust the broader named corpus, which includes Metá Metá, Teto Preto, Kiko Dinucci, hip-hop/electronic artists and cross-generational experiments. Brazilian_indie and brazilian_indie_rock cover national independent fields; neither their selected artist models nor shared members proves exact lexical equivalence. The municipal theatre explicitly names nova música paulista and Tulipa among its protagonists, while the actual creator100 supplies the broad named discovery scope. No exclusive sonic signature, birth-place-only identity, or alternate-arrangement-only distinction is claimed.

tradition.name: Modern Alternative Pop
tradition.lineage: Modern alternative pop brings intimate songwriting together with independent acoustic and electronic production. Artists move between fragile piano-led songs and more layered arrangements, drawing on indie rock, ambient electronics and contemporary popular-song forms.

extras.description: Soft piano and restrained singing can expose the melody and emotional detail of a song. Other arrangements expand the same intimate writing through synthesizers, bass, programmed beats and layered vocal harmonies.

tradition.name: Dangdut Remix
tradition.lineage: Indonesian dance-remix practice reshaping dangdut recordings through digital editing, rhythmic replacement and sampled cross-genre additions. It developed within the cassette and studio-production economy of the 1990s and continues in electronic dance circulation.

extras.description: Dangdut melodies and ornamented singing are placed over reworked electronic dance rhythms. Producers cut and layer recorded fragments, replace or reinforce percussion, and add rhythmic calls, rap or other borrowed textures. The remix is a production practice with varied grooves rather than one fixed drum pattern or exclusively live band format.

tradition.name: Pinoy city pop
tradition.lineage: Filipino city pop connects the renewed international interest in Japanese city pop with Manila Sound, indie songwriting and local pop audiences. Contemporary bands draw on polished jazz-pop harmony, disco-funk rhythm and the melodic warmth of earlier Filipino popular music.

extras.description: Clean guitar figures, rounded bass lines, keyboard chords and a steady kit groove support smooth, tuneful singing. Romantic songwriting and a buoyant retro-modern sound link the Filipino scene to the wider city-pop revival while retaining its own language and musical references.

entries.geo_rationale: Band scene anchor positively named in issuer publicity, not an assertion of exclusive genre geography.
entries.model_policy: Representative Filipino city-pop band practice: melodic pop vocal, clean electric guitar, electric bass, acoustic drum kit and electronic keyboard. Firsthand ALYSON interview positively documents this core configuration and the deliberate synthesis of Japanese city pop with Manila Sound. This is a genre-level compact-band rendition, not a transcription of DEFINITELY LOVE, AFTER OURS or an expanded concert; optional brass/guest singers in those productions are not claimed absent. Authored smooth crooning, syllabic legato, functional-harmonic verse-chorus-bridge organization, clean strums, fingerstyle bass and disco four-beat kit give a coherent pop/funk branch. Alder solid-body guitar and bass, standard strings, maple kit and live-room are representative construction/capture choices, not measured artist equipment. Keyboard architecture remains genuinely unspecified. All applicable owner controls retained; shared alder and amplifier pins apply to both plucked instruments. The retained bass is a fingerstyle locked pop/funk groove with clear percussive attack and controlled fundamental decay. The samul-percussive lexicon contains generic fast-attack/percussive/focused-low-end vocabulary and no compulsory Korean percussion mechanism or repertoire note; in this actual electric-bass context it need not assert a foreign instrument. This is an interpretation of the existing authored sound, not a new performer biography or change of technique. The selected2024 firsthand core-band practice is distinct from the later2026 expanded orchestra event; the later source identifies additional rhythm-guitar/backing-singing roles, neither imported into nor falsely denied for the earlier representative arrangement.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Full city_pop centers Japanese late1970s/1980s urban adult pop and its rediscovery; this contemporary Filipino revival explicitly reworks that influence with local Manila Sound/indie context. Full manila_sound is the historical1973–1980 movement, which remains an influence rather than a renamed modern scene. OPM and Pinoy indie are broad inclusive umbrellas; this is a narrower transnational stylistic revival within them, not exclusion or distinction based only on artist nationality. Firsthand interview explains deliberate difference from Japanese models and broader global movement participation.

tradition.lineage: Philly drill developed within Philadelphia’s contemporary rap community through local MC networks and producers working both in the city and abroad. Sparse, ominous beats and forceful vocal delivery connect it to drill while choral and cinematic sampling give parts of the scene a distinctive atmosphere.

extras.description: Direct rap delivery meets spare programmed percussion, deep 808 bass and ominous sampled textures. Choral, operatic and cinematic fragments can sustain a dark backdrop, while the performers’ local references and cadence keep the music grounded in Philadelphia rap.

tradition.name: Cumbia
tradition.lineage: Cumbia grew from Colombia’s Caribbean musical traditions into a transnational Latin American dance repertoire. Recordings, radio, touring orchestras and migrant audiences carried it across borders, where local communities reshaped its rhythms, instrumentation and social meanings.

extras.description: Repeating bass and percussion patterns support sung refrains and answering instrumental phrases. Dance-orchestra arrangements combine keyboards and brass, while guitar-led, accordion-led and electronic approaches give the wider repertoire distinct regional textures.
